title: Large tenant multipart upload causing retry-echo and session-affinity leak: investigation & targeted fix
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary:
A Tier-1 customer reported repeated 5xx waves and elevated tail latency while uploading large multipart payloads (~50-200MB parts) via the Hosted API. Symptoms included duplicated retries from the client, partial stream replays at the proxy layer, and persistent sticky affinity mapping that caused subsequent requests from other tenants to hit degraded hosts. The incident correlates with a rolling update on a subset of hosts and a change to the edge proxy connection reuse behavior.

Goal:
Identify the chain of failures (client retry amplification, proxy-level stream replay, session-affinity/sticky routing leak), produce a minimal, targeted patch to prevent request duplication and clear stale affinity entries, and ship a monitoring + rollback plan to prevent recurrence during customer-facing maintenance windows.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate a multipart upload client that splits payloads into 100MB parts and concurrently streams parts with HTTP/1.1 chunked uploads.
2) Configure a host pool with one subset under simulated rolling upgrade (introduce 200ms scheduling pause on acceptors).
3) Use SDK retry policy mirroring customer's config: 2 retries with exponential backoff starting at 250ms and idempotency disabled for streaming endpoints.
4) Observe edge proxy logs for repeated Full request bodies being forwarded after connection resets and check affinity map for entries tied to old connection IDs.
5) Measure 5xx counts and token-level latency distribution for tenant during test runs.
observations: Edge proxy replays complete request bodies on socket teardown when backend returns a half-closed stream, leading to duplicate downstream requests.
Affinity table uses a connection-derived key that is not garbage-collected on backend restart, causing new client connections to be routed to warmed-but-partially-degraded hosts.
SDK retry semantics combined with non-idempotent streaming endpoints resulted in client-side retries that retriggered server work because proxy replay occurred before client observed final status.
KV cache eviction churn during the rolling update increased cold-start latency, exacerbating client timeouts and retry windows.
root_cause_summary: Three-fold interaction: (1) edge proxy replay-on-teardown behavior forwards full payloads on specific reset paths; (2) session-affinity keys survived backend lifecycle events and mis-routed new sessions; (3) client retry policy for long multipart uploads was non-idempotent and retried before end-to-end determinism could be guaranteed. The combination produced amplified work and transient 5xx errors for the tenant, and a secondary cross-tenant impact due to sticky routing leak.
proposed_fix:
1) Patch edge proxy to disable replay of full request bodies on the reset path for non-idempotent endpoints; instead return a deterministic 5xx and surface clear retry guidance in headers.
2) Update affinity table GC: add backend-life-version to keys and TTL-based eager eviction on backend restart signals to avoid routing to partially degraded hosts.
3) Ship an SDK advisory/guardrail: detect large streaming uploads and temporarily switch to a streaming-safe idempotency token or escalate to a resumable upload flow.
4) Add server-side de-duplication token check for recent request hashes within a short window (60s) to mitigate unavoidable duplicates during rollout.
rollout_plan: A. Canary patch to edge proxy on 5% of traffic in us-west-2 with strict telemetry hooks (3h canary).
B. Concurrent backend affinity GC change behind feature flag; gradually enable across regions after canary success.
C. Customer-facing SDK advisory + opt-in client update for resumable uploads; share migration guide with affected customers in parallel.
D. Deploy short-window server-side dedupe as emergency mitigation before client-side adoption completes.
E. Full global rollout after 48h stable telemetry and no new duplication incidents.
monitoring_and_checks: Dashboard: request duplication ratio (proxy-forward-count / unique-request-id) by tenant.
Metric: affinity-table-size and affinity-gc-rate; rollout should not regress GC beyond baseline.
Traces: sample end-to-end traces for multipart endpoints showing duplicate downstream spans.
Runbook step: immediate rollback of proxy patch if cross-tenant 5xx increases.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy no longer replays full request bodies on reset paths for non-idempotent endpoints in canary region.
Affinity table GC prevents stale routing to workers restarted within the last 5 minutes during canary.
Server-side dedupe reduces duplicate downstream work metric by >= 90% for the reproduced scenario.
No increase in cross-tenant 5xx or latency tail during canary (10% traffic) compared to baseline.
